findings.F1: In the rising calm profile, a one-day fall is followed by a next-day rebound that grows with the fall's size, measured against the coin's 30-day daily swing. The product of the scaled fall and the next day's excess return over all down days averages +0.81 % (t 3.10 with day-clustered errors, 731 cases on 324 days). Outside the profile the same product is weaker: +0.50 %, t 1.81, 3304 cases.
findings.F2: The rebound is graded across bins in the rising calm profile. Days falling more than one usual swing gain +1.62 % excess the next day (t 2.97, 173 cases, 91 days). Smaller falls gain +0.47 % (t 1.81, 560 cases), and up days gain −0.02 % (t −0.05, 624 cases).
findings.F3: The rebound persists past one day. On non-overlapping grids, the graded product in rising calm is +1.07 % over 2 days (t 2.24, 377 cases, 161 days) and +1.96 % over 3 days (t 2.30, 234 cases, 104 days). Falls of more than one swing gain +4.39 % excess over 3 days (t 2.79, 67 cases).
findings.F4: The 5-day horizon the tested idea used shows no effect. The verdict found an unusual move of +0.04 % per case (t 0.09, 1159 cases). Short trades lost −5.33 % on average net (1098 trades), and the shorts paid the profile's drift of about +0.34 % a day. The rebound is concentrated in the first 1–3 days.
findings.F5: The next-day graded product is positive in all 4 years: 2018 +0.50 % (t 0.50), 2019 +0.14 % (t 0.23), 2020 +1.23 % (t 4.73) and 2021 +0.83 % (t 1.47). It is positive in 9 of 10 coins; DOGE is the exception with 8 cases. It is positive in 9 of 12 windows (w15 −0.48 %, t −0.33).
findings.F6: A falling day in the rising calm profile that closes in the top third of its range does not rebound: −0.97 % next day (t −1.43, 68 cases). Falls closing in the lower or middle third gain +0.96 % (t 2.37, 335 cases) and +0.88 % (t 2.97, 328 cases).
findings.F7: Two other patterns stand out in the rising calm profile, and both are already held in the profile map. Thursdays carry a next-day excess of +1.46 % (t 4.69, 229 cases); the map holds this as 045-01, "rising market late week gain". Five-day excess returns are highest at a 5-day closing high (+3.58 %, t 2.81, 97 cases); the map holds this as 034-01.b1 / 035-01.b1, "nearness to high". Neither is proposed again.
findings.F8: The size of the rebound clears the cost of a trade. Next-day excess after falls of more than one swing is +1.62 % (F2), against a cost of 0.22 % per trade, about 7 times the cost before the drift is added.

ideas.idea: In a rising, calm market, the larger a coin's one-day fall against its usual daily swing over the past 30 days, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a calm uptrend can buy a sharp one-day drop for a one-day hold, sized by how large the drop was against the coin's usual swing.
ideas.name: calm uptrend one-day dip rebound

ideas.idea: In a rising, calm market, the larger a coin's one-day fall against its usual daily swing over the past 30 days, the larger its rise over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader can hold a calm-uptrend dip purchase for about three days rather than one, but not as long as five.
ideas.name: calm uptrend dip three-day rebound
